script.title: Clarence Chamberlin beheaded a dragon, then claimed $25 🤯
sentences: Clarence Chamberlin beheaded a dragon with a wingtip.
This was 1931, and Chamberlin, an aviation pioneer, had spotted the dragon midair.
He cut its head off, brought the pieces back to land, and claimed a 25 dollar award.
The dragon was a balloon from the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade.
In 1928, Tony Sarg started letting the parade's helium balloons go on purpose.
They leaked slowly for a week, came down, and whoever found one got a reward.
All but one came back, a blue hippo that drifted past the Empire State Building and was never found.
script.description:
In 1931 a pilot sliced the head off a Macy's parade balloon in midair.
One blue hippo balloon was never found.
claims_en: In 1931 aviation pioneer Clarence Chamberlin spotted a dragon balloon midair
He decapitated it with a wingtip
He brought the remnants back to land
The dragon was a Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade balloon
In 1928 Macy's switched to helium and Tony Sarg released the balloons; the practice continued until 1932
The released balloons were set to leak slowly over a week and then descend
All but one balloon were recovered
A blue hippopotamus balloon drifted southeast past the Empire State Building after the 1931 parade and was never found
scenes: Extreme close-up of a 1930s aviator in leather flying helmet and goggles, face frozen in astonished determination, cockpit wind whipping, cold autumn sky light
A 1931 open-cockpit biplane banking over New York rooftops toward a huge green dragon-shaped parade balloon floating in a grey November sky, wide shot

The biplane's wingtip slicing through the neck of the floating dragon balloon, fabric tearing away, the pilot gritting his teeth, dramatic side angle; then the aviator on a small airfield holding torn balloon fabric as an official hands him a few dollar bills
A 1930s Macy's Thanksgiving parade on a New York street, giant animal balloons over crowds in coats and hats, festive daylight
A puppeteer in a 1920s suit and bow tie grinning as he lets go of the ropes of giant helium animal balloons rising over a city street, low angle
Children in a 1930s countryside field running toward a deflated animal balloon that has drifted down onto the grass, soft morning light
A large blue hippopotamus balloon drifting alone past the Empire State Building at dusk, tiny in the vast sky, melancholy wide shot
